title: Docs: Shadow Traffic (Shadow Evals) beta enablement, metrics interpretation, and limitations
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Internal docs for Shadow Evals beta: how to enable shadow traffic per-route, how to interpret shadow_eval metrics and dashboards, and clearly documented safety/compliance limitations (retention/redaction, SLO boundaries, quotas, kill switch).
commits: docs(shadow-evals): add overview + enablement guide for beta
docs(observability): add shadow_eval metrics reference + tagging notes
docs(security): document retention/redaction defaults and customer controls
docs(console): add dashboard walkthrough + filter semantics
docs(oncall): add kill switch + alert runbook entry points
chore(mkdocs): add nav entries + fix broken links
description: Summary: Adds internal documentation for the Shadow Traffic / “Shadow Evals” beta (how to enable per-route shadowing, how to interpret quality + performance metrics, and what beta limitations/guardrails apply). The goal is to unblock Console rollout users and internal oncall/support by putting the most common questions in one place and aligning terminology across Product, Telemetry, SRE, and Security. Context: Shadow Traffic mirrors a sampled subset of live requests to one or more shadow targets and runs them asynchronously; results must never block or alter the primary response. Docs here focus on: (1) enabling/disabling shadowing safely, (2) understanding metrics and dashboards, (3) data handling/retention + redaction, and (4) operational boundaries (budgets, rate limits, kill switch, and what pages/alerts mean). Related work: PM-612 (beta plan/GA criteria), ENG-2420 (RoutePolicy schema), ENG-2431/2432 (Console API/UI), ENG-2435 (cardinality guardrails), ENG-2443 (kill switch). What’s included (high level): Overview page that explains request mirroring, linking via request_id, and common use cases (candidate model comparison, quantization profile validation, prompt/config changes). Enablement guide with examples of RoutePolicy shadow_traffic fields (sampling %, allowlist, region constraints, shadow targets) and a “safe defaults” section. Metrics reference that defines shadow_eval.* signals, required dimensions, and how to read judge win-rate vs format adherence vs safety outcomes, plus latency/cost deltas (shadow-only). Beta limitations page that explicitly calls out: not a replacement for offline evals; judge scores are comparative signals not ground truth; traffic representativeness caveats; strict SLO boundaries (primary p99 must not regress; shadow failures should be isolated); and known blind spots (low sample sizes, high-cardinality tags dropped/bucketed). Security/retention page describing default retention (short-lived by default), redaction behavior for prompts/outputs, data residency constraints, and customer opt-out controls; also clarifies that payload access is restricted and audited. Console dashboard walkthrough with definitions of filters and breakdowns (route/model/region/time window) and recommended alert thresholds to watch during beta. Oncall runbook snippets: kill switch paths (global + per-route), verification queries/dashboards to confirm shadowing is off, and comms checklist pointers. Notes: I intentionally avoided including any customer-identifying examples in the docs. All examples use synthetic route names and fake model ids. I also aligned naming to “Shadow Evals” in Console while keeping “shadow traffic” for the data-plane mechanism. Checklist: - [x] Link check passes (mkdocs + CI link checker) - [x] Metrics names match current telemetry spec (shadow_eval.*) - [x] Security language reviewed for SOC2 posture (retention, access controls, auditability) - [x] Kill switch docs match current admin endpoint naming - [x] Console screenshots removed (UI is still moving; used annotated placeholders + callouts instead) Follow-ups (not in this PR): Add a short “How to gate rollouts using shadow thresholds” page once ENG-48347 ships broadly; we currently reference it as “coming during beta” with a pointer to PM-612 for internal tracking.
review_conversation: Marissa Cole (review): Can we be explicit that shadow runs never impact the primary response, even if the shadow target times out? Also please align the customer-facing name to “Shadow Evals” (Console) but keep “shadow traffic” as the underlying mechanism. (requested changes)

Elliot Price (author): Updated overview + beta limitations to call out: shadow execution is async, best-effort, and cannot block/alter primary response; timeouts/drops are shadow-only. Also updated headings to use “Shadow Evals” consistently, with a glossary entry mapping to “shadow traffic”.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics page: please add the cardinality guardrails. Specifically: which tags are allowed, and what happens when a disallowed tag appears. We should say we bucket/strip and increment a drop/bucket counter. (requested changes)

Elliot Price (author): Added a “Cardinality & tagging rules” section (allowed dimensions, bucketing behavior, and which counters to watch). Also linked to ENG-2435 so readers know where the enforcement lives.

Sean Gallagher (review): Oncall section: add explicit guidance on what alerts page (queue depth + shadow drop counts) and the expected response is. Also reiterate that primary SLO is the priority; if in doubt, disable shadowing. (requested changes)

Elliot Price (author): Added an “Oncall decision tree” subsection and a one-line policy: primary-path health > shadow signal completeness. Included disable steps (per-route first, then global) and verification checks.

Naomi Feldman (review): Security page needs to be more careful: don’t imply we store raw prompts/outputs by default. Make default retention and redaction explicit, and mention restricted access + audit trails for any payload sampling. (requested changes)

Elliot Price (author): Updated security wording: default is minimal retention with redaction; storing payload samples requires explicit configuration + restricted access and is audited. Removed any ambiguous phrasing.
Chloe Martin (review): Enablement examples: can we include one example with multiple shadow targets and clarify how results appear (separate target_id breakdown)? (comment)
Elliot Price (author): Added a multi-target example and a note on “target_id” as the key breakdown in Console/metrics.
Paula Mendes (review): Beta limitations: please add a note that low sample sizes make win-rate noisy; recommend minimum n before gating. (comment)
Elliot Price (author): Added a “Minimum sample guidance” box (n thresholds + confidence caveats) and recommended using hold/alerting instead of automatic rollback until thresholds are met.
Marissa Cole (final): LGTM after edits. Approved.
Naomi Feldman (final): Approved with the updated retention/redaction language.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved; oncall guidance looks good.
Allison Grant (final): Approved; metrics/tagging alignment looks consistent.
